title: DS-CORE: strengthen evals per traceability review 2026-10-06
summary: Fixes the 15 weak requirement→eval links found by the semantic review: splits overloaded tests, adds missing negative/partition/load conditions, removes a duplicate eval, and closes a false-proof in the erasure eval.
rationale: Traceability evaluation 2026-10-06 passed narrowly (semantic 0.81; REQ-0012 at 0.5). Fixing eval definitions now is cheaper than after code exists.

impact_notes.stories: Updates evals on 15 stories (STORY-0001, 0006, 0007, 0008, 0010, 0012, 0017, 0018, 0023, 0025, 0027, 0029, 0031, 0032, 0036). No story scope, requirement or task changes.
impact_notes.code: No code exists yet. Test names the tasks must create change, e.g. server/tests/{raft,txn,graph_model,limits,gql_negative,audit,security,telemetry}.rs and harness subcommands (erasure --reader decrypting, import-resume, telemetry --nodes 3). Task done_when texts still read 'story evals pass'.
impact_notes.evals: Net +13 evals (57 → 70): 1 duplicate driver conformance eval removed from STORY-0031, 14 added; the REQ-0013 boundary check moves to integration with a performance eval kept for the quality gate.
risks: More evals lengthen the acceptance and performance stages; Jepsen and 30-minute performance runs should run nightly rather than per commit.
STORY-0031 E2 needs RELEASE_VERSION from the release pipeline (post-deploy stage).
